phases.title: Make the test harness capable of failing
phases.finding: src/testing/harness.rs:execute_test_code() returns Ok(()) unless the code fails to parse or throws, so a Redblue test can only fail by crashing - no assertion is ever evaluated. src/testing/assertions.rs (19 assertion fns) is dead code, reachable only via `pub use assertions::*` in testing/mod.rs:6. Verified deeper than first recorded: Expr::Expect is declared at parser.rs:56 but there is NO construction site anywhere in parser.rs, so the `expect A to be B` form does not merely go unasserted, it fails to parse - ParserError: Unexpected token Expect. `rb test` reports 0 tests because every .rb file in tests/ is 100% commented out and discovery only matches lines starting `// test `.

a correct test (expect 1 to be 1) PASSES
cargo test proves both directions

phases.finding: src/vm.rs has no frame or recursion counter (grep for depth|stack|limit in vm.rs returns only a string-splitting depth at line 990). Infinite or deep recursion aborts the process with a Rust stack overflow instead of a clean Runtime error.
phases.goal: Add a configurable call-depth limit producing a catchable Runtime error.

infinite recursion -> RuntimeError, process exit code 1, no abort

phases.title: Numeric edge semantics

phases.title: Make `break` and `skip` leave the loop instead of silently doing nothing
phases.finding: src/vm.rs:517-523 — `Statement::Break` and `Statement::Skip` each carry `// TODO: Implement proper control flow` and evaluate to `Ok(Value::Nothing)`. No loop consults them: `for each` (src/vm.rs:460), `repeat N times` (src/vm.rs:489) and `while` (src/vm.rs:505) all run their body to completion. Verified against the built binary: `for each i in [1,2,3] / if i is 2 then break end / say i / end` prints 1 2 3 and exits 0, and the same program with a `break` after `set n to n + 1` inside `repeat 5 times` still reports n = 5. SPEC.md:417-433 documents both statements with worked examples (`if i is 50 / break / end`), GRAMMAR.md:245-246 lists them, and src/lexer.rs:19-20 reserves the words while src/parser.rs:433-441 parses them — so the language accepts a program that compiles, runs, exits 0 and gives the WRONG ANSWER. Worse, two green tests pin the broken behaviour as correct: tests/test_lists.rb:108 `test "lists: break inside a loop does not truncate it"` asserts `expect total to be 10` where a working `break` at value 3 would make it 3, and tests/test_lists.rb:92 `test "lists: a conditional inside a loop does not disturb the iteration"` asserts `expect seen to be 4` where a working `skip` at value 2 would make it 3. A silent no-op that reports success is the most expensive class of defect this pipeline can ship.
phases.goal: Make `break` exit the innermost enclosing loop and `skip` advance to its next iteration, in `for each`, `repeat N times` and `while`, and correct the two Redblue tests that currently assert the broken behaviour.
accept: `for each i in [1,2,3] / if i is 2 then break end / say i / end` exits 0 and prints 1 only
`for each i in [1,2,3] / if i is 2 then skip end / say i / end` exits 0 and prints 1 then 3

the same two programs behave identically inside `repeat N times` and inside `while`, and a `break` in the body of a nested loop leaves only the INNER loop — an outer loop with its own counter keeps counting, pinned by a test

tests/test_lists.rb:92 and tests/test_lists.rb:108 are CORRECTED, not deleted: both are rewritten to assert the real semantics (`seen` is 3 with a working `skip`, `total` is 3 with a working `break` at value 3), and a test asserts those two named tests still exist and still pass

edge tests named edge_* cover: `break`/`skip` as the first statement of a body, as the last, inside an `if` nested two blocks deep, in a loop whose body is a single statement, and `skip` on the final iteration of a `for each`

edge tests assert a FAILURE for `break` and for `skip` outside any loop — a clean caught RuntimeError naming the statement, not a silent no-op and not a panic; both must also be catchable with `try`/`catch error` inside a loop
the iteration budget is charged and released exactly as an uninterrupted iteration does, so `cargo test --all-targets` reports 0 failures including the 22 tests in tests/loop_bounds_test.rs
`cargo test --all-targets` reports 0 failures and every file in examples/ and modules/ exits 0 (MathUtils.rb excepted, baselined until phase-024)

phases.title: Lex the comparison symbols `<` `>` `=` `!` so the comparison parser is reachable
phases.finding: src/lexer.rs:398 is the operator table (`let kind = match c`) and it has arms for `+ - * / % ( ) [ ] { } , . :` only; the `_ =>` arm at src/lexer.rs:446 raises `Unexpected character '{c}'`. There is no arm for `<`, `>`, `=` or `!`, so `if x > 10` fails with `LexerError: Unexpected character '>'`. Consequently TokenKind::Equal/NotEqual/Less/LessEqual/Greater/GreaterEqual (declared src/lexer.rs:137-144) are NEVER constructed by the lexer: `grep -rn 'TokenKind::Less\|TokenKind::Greater\|TokenKind::Equal\|TokenKind::NotEqual' src/*.rs` matches only src/parser.rs:1183-1258, i.e. the whole comparison arm block in parse_comparison is unreachable code. README.md:18 (`if count is greater than 10`), SPEC.md:277-282 (`>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `==`, `!=`) and docs/GRAMMAR.md:93-98 all document these forms as working. Consequence: the language has NO ordering comparison at all — `x > y`, `x < y`, `x == y`, `x != y` are all lex errors today.
phases.goal: Make `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `==`, `!=` lex into the TokenKind variants the parser already handles, so ordering comparison is reachable in the language.
accept: `cargo test` is green and a new test runs a .rb file containing `if x > 10 then`, `if x >= 10 then`, `if x < 10 then`, `if x <= 10 then`, `if x == 10 then` and `if x != 10 then` through `rb run` and asserts exit 0 with the branch it selects
a lexer test pins each of `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `==`, `!=` to its exact TokenKind, and `<=`/`>=` are one token rather than two

edge tests named edge_* cover: the equality boundary in both directions (`x < x` is no, `x <= x` is yes, `x > x` is no, `x >= x` is yes), reversed operands, and `==` on two lists and two records that hold equal contents

edge tests assert a FAILURE for ordering two operands of different types (`1 < "a"`, `yes >= 3`) and for ordering a list against a number — the result must be a caught RuntimeError, never a `yes` and never a panic
no existing behaviour regresses: `cargo test --all-targets` reports 0 failures and every file in examples/ and modules/ still exits 0 (MathUtils.rb excepted, it stays baselined until phase-024)
SPEC.md and docs/GRAMMAR.md are left stating what the code now does

phases.title: Parse the English comparison forms `is greater than` / `is less than` / `is equal to`
phases.finding: src/parser.rs:1170 `fn parse_comparison` handles `TokenKind::Is` at src/parser.rs:1176-1198 by looking only for a following `TokenKind::Equal` (1182-1187) or `TokenKind::Not` (1188-1193) and otherwise falling through to `BinaryOp::Equal` at 1196-1197. `greater`, `less`, `than`, `to` and `or` are plain identifiers, so `if x is greater than 10 then` consumes `greater` as the right operand of `is` and then fails with `ParserError: Expected Then but got Identifier("than")`. `if x is equal to 1 then` fails with `Expected Then but got To`. Six of the seven documented comparison spellings in README.md:18, SPEC.md:273-274, SPEC.md:281-282, ROADMAP.md:10 and docs/GRAMMAR.md:93-98 therefore do not parse; only bare `is` (equality) and `is not` work. This is the flagship example of README.md:18 and of ROADMAP.md:10.
phases.goal: Make `is greater than`, `is greater than or equal to`, `is less than`, `is less than or equal to`, `is equal to` and `is not` parse, matching what README.md, SPEC.md and docs/GRAMMAR.md already promise.
accept: a new test runs a .rb file using all six word forms through `rb run`, asserts exit 0, and asserts which branch each one took
the word forms agree with the symbolic forms added in phase-025 on the same inputs: `x is greater than y` and `x > y` select the same branch for equal, greater, less, and non-comparable operands
`is greater than or equal to` binds looser than `is greater than`, so `x is greater than or equal to y` is not parsed as `(x is greater than y) or equal to y` — a test pins that specifically
edge tests named edge_* cover: the equality boundary in both directions, both operands in reversed order, and operands that are lists or records
edge tests assert a FAILURE for ordering a number against text and a record against a number — a caught RuntimeError, not a `yes` and not a panic
`cargo test --all-targets` reports 0 failures and every file in examples/ and modules/ still exits 0 (MathUtils.rb excepted, baselined until phase-024)

phases.title: Implement the range loop `for each i from A to B [by C]`
phases.finding: src/parser.rs:651 `fn parse_for` has exactly one arm — `TokenKind::Each` at src/parser.rs:656 — and it unconditionally calls `self.expect(&TokenKind::In)?` at src/parser.rs:676 before parsing the iterable. There is no `from A to B [by C]` arm and no `by` step. `for each i from 1 to 3` therefore fails with `ParserError: Expected In but got From`, and so does every range loop in README.md:101-103, SPEC.md:380-391 and docs/GRAMMAR.md:222. Statement::ForEach (src/parser.rs:696) carries no bounds, so the VM has nothing to iterate. This is the single most common loop in the language's own README and it does not run. Note that phase-025 and phase-026 must land first: a range loop over a numeric boundary is untestable without `<`, `>` and `is greater than`.
phases.goal: Make `for each i from A to B`, `for each i from A to B by C` parse and run, with the iteration count bounded by the same MAX_ITERATIONS guard every other loop uses.
accept: `rb run` of a file with `for each i from 1 to 5` exits 0 and prints 1 2 3 4 5 once each, in order
`for each i from 0 to 10 by 5` visits 0, 5, 10 and nothing else; `by 1` and an omitted `by` agree
the loop variable is a local: setting it inside the body does not change the sequence, and it is out of scope after `end` (an AnalyzerError, not a silent global)

edge tests named edge_* cover: an empty range (`from 5 to 1` visits nothing and does not hang), a single-iteration range (`from 3 to 3`), a descending `by`, a fractional `by` on a whole-number range, and `from`/`to`/`by` given a non-number (a clean RuntimeError naming the argument)
edge tests assert a FAILURE for `by 0` (infinite loop) — it must stop with a RuntimeError naming MAX_ITERATIONS, not hang and not abort
the existing iteration guard is reused rather than bypassed: a range whose length exceeds the configured MAX_ITERATIONS stops with the same RuntimeError a `repeat N times` gives
`cargo test --all-targets` reports 0 failures and every file in examples/ and modules/ still exits 0 (MathUtils.rb excepted, baselined until phase-024)

phases.title: Make `mod` a keyword and implement the `in` membership operator
phases.finding: `In,` is a `BinaryOp` variant at src/parser.rs:86 but is never constructed anywhere in src/ — `grep -rn 'BinaryOp::In' src/` returns nothing — so `if "a" is in words then` fails with `ParserError: Unexpected token In`, though SPEC.md:325 and docs/GRAMMAR.md:372 both document it. Separately, `mod` is absent from the KEYWORDS table at src/lexer.rs:14-60 and the lexer only maps the symbol form `'%' => TokenKind::Mod` at src/lexer.rs:413, so SPEC.md:206 (`set remainder to 10 mod 3`) and docs/GRAMMAR.md:90 fail with `AnalyzerError: Unknown variable 'mod'` — a misleading message, because the source is well-formed Redblue. No file in examples/, modules/ or tests/ uses `mod` as an identifier (verified: `grep -rn '\bmod\b' examples/*.rb modules/*.rb tests/*.rb` is empty), so reserving the word cannot break an existing program.

phases.title: Implement the `unless` block the lexer already reserves

phases.title: Implement `module ... end`, `export`, and the `import X as Y` alias
phases.finding: `("module", TokenKind::Module)` is at src/lexer.rs:43 and `("export", TokenKind::Export)` at src/lexer.rs:45, and SPEC.md:618-648 plus docs/GRAMMAR.md:143-157 document a full module system. Neither token has an arm in the statement dispatch at src/parser.rs:420 (`grep -c 'TokenKind::Module\|TokenKind::Export' src/parser.rs` is 0 each): `module M ... end` fails with `ParserError: Unexpected token Module`. `import` IS handled (src/parser.rs:465) but the `as` alias it parses at src/parser.rs:501 is never bound, so `import json as J` then `J.parse("{}")` fails with `AnalyzerError: Unknown variable 'as'` and `Unknown variable 'J'`. Nothing in the repo exercises a module declaration: neither modules/MathUtils.rb nor modules/SuiteKit.rb contains the word `module`, so the `examples/` sweep in rbops/verify.sh:225 has never run one.

phases.title: Reconcile the stdlib module list in SPEC.md with src/stdlib.rs

Worse, 333 of the REPL's 730 lines are unreachable: `ReplCommand` (src/repl/commands.rs:1), `ReplCompleter` (src/repl/completer.rs:1) and `ReplHistory` (src/repl/history.rs:3) are declared and re-exported at src/repl/mod.rs:9-11 but never constructed anywhere — `Repl` keeps its own `history: Vec<String>` (src/repl/mod.rs:18) and re-parses the command word by hand at src/repl/mod.rs:78-84, duplicating the table already written at src/repl/commands.rs:32-83. `ReplHistory::search`, `search_all`, `save_to_file` and `load_from_file` (src/repl/history.rs:32-87) have no caller at all, so the history-file format is unexercised. clippy stays silent because all three types are `pub`.

phases.title: Add the function literal `to (x) ... end` as an expression
phases.finding: `Expr` (src/parser.rs:5-68) has Number, Text, YesNo, Nothing, Variable, Binary, Unary, Call, Property, MethodCall, Index, InterpolatedText, List, Record and Expect — and no function-literal variant, while docs/GRAMMAR.md:413-419 specifies `function_literal = 'to' [ '(' parameter { ',' parameter } ')' ] { statement } 'end'` and SPEC.md:484-491 shows `set double to to (x) give back x * 2`. `to` is only accepted as a statement (src/parser.rs:461 `TokenKind::To => self.parse_function()?`) and never as a primary expression, so `set double to to (x) give back x * 2` fails with `ParserError: Unexpected token To`, and so does `[1,2,3].map(to (x) give back x * 2)`. SPEC.md:496-502's `give back to ... end` counter form is equally unreachable. Closures themselves work — phase-011 landed capture and tests/closure_capture_test.rs has 26 passing tests — but only through a NAMED nested `to name() ... end` declaration, so there is no way to write a higher-order function at all, and SPEC.md:785's `list.map` example can never run.
phases.goal: Add a function literal to the AST and the grammar so an anonymous function is a value, closing the gap between the working named-closure behaviour and what SPEC.md documents.
accept: `rb run` of a file with `set double to to (x) give back x * 2` followed by `say double(21)` exits 0 and prints 42

the literal captures its enclosing bindings by value at the point it is written, matching the policy pinned by tests/closure_capture_test.rs:17-22 — a closure defined inside a function sees that function's locals, not the caller's

phases.title: Remove the reachable panics in the time builtins
phases.finding: src/vm.rs:924, src/vm.rs:1089, src/vm.rs:1238, src/vm.rs:1250 and src/vm.rs:1263 each call `SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap()`. `duration_since` returns `Err(SystemTimeError)` for any instant before 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z and `.unwrap()` on it panics. All five sit inside the time builtins, reachable from a plain Redblue program through `time.now()` with no test, no flag and no unusual input — only a host clock set before the epoch. Every other error path in those functions is a RuntimeError; these five unwind through the interpreter thread and abort the process. This is the reachable-`unwrap` class the reviewer contract (AGENTS.md section 5) names as a hunt target, and it is the only place in src/ where `.unwrap()` appears outside test code — the other 7 unwraps are all in `mod tests` blocks.
phases.goal: Turn the five clock unwraps into RuntimeErrors, so no Redblue program can panic the interpreter through a host clock set before the Unix epoch.
accept: no `.unwrap()` remains in src/ outside a `#[cfg(test)]` or `mod tests` block, and `grep -rn 'unwrap()' src/` is pasted into REPORT.md showing only test lines

the five call sites report a caught RuntimeError naming the clock rather than panicking, and a Redblue `try`/`catch error` around a failing `time.now()` yields the error instead of aborting the process

the failure is exercised WITHOUT moving the machine clock: the seconds-since-epoch conversion is extracted behind a function that takes the instant as an argument, so a test passes a pre-epoch instant directly and asserts the error — the test is deterministic and does not depend on wall-clock state
edge tests named edge_* cover a pre-epoch instant, the exact epoch boundary, and `time.format` given an argument that is not a number or not a text
